title: On the origin of nonreciprocal charge transport in topological insulator BiSbTeSe2
authors: Fengyi Guo, Ziqi Wang, Xiubing Li, Zheng Dai, Congcong Li, Yufan Ju, Shuai Zhang, Bin Cheng, Zhe Ying, Fengqi Song
abstract: Nonreciprocal charge transport provides an effective approach for probing direction dependent charge dynamics and spin-momentum-locked electronic states. Here, we report highly gate-tunable nonreciprocal charge transport in dual-gated BiSbTeSe2 topological insulator device. The second-harmonic longitudinal resistance is linear in both current and magnetic field. The nonreciprocal response reaches its maximum near the charge neutrality point, exhibits sign reversals on either side, and is strongly suppressed once the Fermi level enters the bulk states. We suggest that the nonreciprocal response is attributed to the inhomogeneity of spin-momentum locking in the topological surface states. The nonreciprocal signal near the charge neutrality point is about one order of magnitude larger than that without gate modulation and remains robust up to 300 K, highlighting BiSbTeSe2 as a promising platform for room-temperature nonlinear electronics.
summary: This work reports on highly tunable nonreciprocal charge transport in $	ext{BiSbTeSe}_2$ topological insulators using a dual-gated device. The nonreciprocal signal is maximized near the charge neutrality point and is attributed to spin-momentum locking inhomogeneities in the surface states. The findings highlight $	ext{BiSbTeSe}_2$ as a promising platform for room-temperature nonlinear electronics.
main_problem: The study investigates the origin and control of nonreciprocal charge transport (NCT) in topological insulators, specifically focusing on the dependence of transport on direction and gate voltage.
main_result: The nonreciprocal response is strongly enhanced near the charge neutrality point and is attributed to scattering mechanisms arising from the inhomogeneity of spin-momentum locking within the topological surface states.
method: Transport measurements were performed using dual-gated $	ext{BiSbTeSe}_2$ devices, measuring the second-harmonic longitudinal resistance ($R_{xx}^{2\omega}$) while varying gate voltages, magnetic fields, and temperature.
model_or_system: The physical system is a dual-gated $	ext{BiSbTeSe}_2$ topological insulator flake, which hosts topologically protected surface states (TSSs). The analysis decomposes the total nonreciprocal response into contributions from the top and bottom surfaces.
key_observables: Nonreciprocal resistance ($R_{xx}^{2\omega}$), nonreciprocal coefficient ($\gamma$), and the dependence of these quantities on gate voltages ($V_{tg}, V_{bg}$), magnetic field ($B$), and temperature ($T$).
important_parameters: The maximum nonreciprocal response is observed near the charge neutrality point (CNP); the response remains robust up to 300 K.
main_assumptions: The nonreciprocal response is highly sensitive to the imbalance between the top and bottom surface contributions, and the mechanism is linked to inhomogeneous spin-momentum locking.
figures_summary: Figures map the gate-dependent nonreciprocal resistance, show linear dependence on current and magnetic field, and illustrate the angular dependence of the response, confirming the CNP maximum.
paper_structure: The paper systematically presents measurements showing the gate-tunability of NCT, analyzes its dependence on magnetic field and temperature, and finally attributes the observed behavior to specific scattering mechanisms within the TSSs.
why_interesting: While focused on condensed matter transport, the study of non-linear, direction-dependent transport phenomena in topological materials touches upon concepts of broken symmetries and chiral dynamics that are relevant to advanced quantum device physics.
